flagged: Vitruvius wrote the "single stone mass… every day stronger" quote (narration) (false: The author is Pliny the Elder (Natural History 35.166). Vitruvius wrote about the same volcanic ash (De Architectura 2.6.1) but not these words.)

Cosa has the oldest or earliest surviving concrete made to set underwater (narration, caption, on-screen text) (disputed: The ROMACONS team's 2004 report still called Cosa the earliest known. Their 2014 book, Building for Eternity, weakened that claim. It says the harbour concrete is probably from the time of Augustus, and that the oldest datable site is the Portus Iulius channel (37 BC). Suggested wording: "among the earliest known.")

The concrete dates to the "second or first century BC" / "late 2nd or 1st century BC" (narration, caption, on-screen text) (disputed: Not hedged: it gives a range but uses no hedging words. The late-2nd-century date comes from the excavations of the 1970s and 80s. A carbon date from core PCO.2003.01 gives 57 BC–AD 33, which points to the second or third quarter of the 1st century BC. The 2014 book says about 60 BC to the Augustan period. Suggested wording: "1st century BC.")
The cores were drilled in 1993 (narration) (false: Drilling was in June 2003. The ROMACONS project wasn't set up until 2001.)
ROMACONS took six cores (on-screen text, about Cosa) (false: False as presented here. Six cores came from the whole 2003 season. One was from Santa Liberata, so five were from Cosa.)

The cores were 0.48–2.25 m (about 1.5–7.4 ft) long, "up to about 7 feet" (narration, on-screen text) (unsupported: Unsupported for Cosa specifically. Hedged with "about" and "up to". The range is correct for the whole 2003 season, and the foot conversions are right. The sources don't show the 2.25 m core came from Cosa. For Cosa Pier 1, the hole was 2.23 m deep and the recovered core was 1.65 m.)

The cracks sealed within 60 days (narration) (unsupported: No source gives 60 days. The paper says water flow stopped after 30 days, and MIT's press release says two weeks. Change this to 30 days to match the caption.)

Cosa's concrete hasn't been tested for hot mixing / "Nobody has checked" (narration, caption, on-screen text) (unsupported: I found no hot-mixing study of Cosa, but that doesn't prove there isn't one. Building for Eternity already shows lime chunks with cracks in Cosa core PCO.2003.01. Suggested wording: "hasn't been specifically tested for hot mixing, as far as we know.")

"No source backs" the claim that Roman concrete lasts 40 times longer (on-screen text) (unsupported: The search allowance ran out before either the figure or the claim that no source backs it could be checked. Check this separately.)

No surviving text gives a full Roman mixing method (on-screen text) (disputed: Vitruvius (De Architectura 5.12.2) does describe what goes into marine concrete. ROMACONS used that passage to build their replica pier. It isn't a complete recipe, though. Suggested wording: "no surviving text gives every detail.")
